blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

item.vignette: A 12-year-old girl has chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism, and primary adrenal insufficiency. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in AIRE. Her circulating T-cell count is normal.
item.lead_in: Which thymic process is most directly impaired by this genetic defect?

options.A: Positive selection of thymocytes that can recognize self-MHC molecules in the thymic cortex
options.B: Ectopic expression of tissue-restricted self antigens by medullary thymic epithelial cells for deletion of strongly self-reactive T cells
options.C: Somatic recombination of variable, diversity, and joining gene segments during lymphocyte development
options.D: FOXP3-dependent suppression of activated lymphocytes by mature peripheral regulatory T cells
options.E: Immunoglobulin class-switch recombination after CD40 signaling in germinal centers

item.difficulty_basis: Expert estimate only; requires recognition of APECED/AIRE and localization to medullary self-antigen display and central negative selection.
item.tested_construct: AIRE-dependent tissue-restricted self-antigen expression in medullary thymic epithelial cells enables central negative selection

explanation.key_explanation: AIRE promotes expression of tissue-restricted self antigens in medullary thymic epithelial cells. This broad self-antigen display exposes developing thymocytes to peripheral self proteins and supports deletion of strongly self-reactive clones. Loss of AIRE therefore disrupts central tolerance and permits multiorgan autoimmunity.

distractor_explanations.A: Positive selection is a cortical self-MHC-recognition step and is not the defining AIRE-dependent process.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. AIRE-mediated medullary self-antigen display supports negative selection of autoreactive thymocytes.
distractor_explanations.C: V(D)J recombination is performed by the RAG complex, not AIRE.
distractor_explanations.D: FOXP3 is essential for regulatory T-cell production and function, a distinct tolerance mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: CD40L-CD40 signaling drives immunoglobulin class switching in mature B cells, not thymic central tolerance.

explanation.educational_objective: AIRE promotes tissue-restricted self-antigen expression in medullary thymic epithelial cells, enabling central negative selection; loss permits autoreactive T cells to escape and causes APECED.

evidence_map.claim: AIRE-mediated medullary self-antigen display supports central tolerance and deletion of strongly self-reactive thymocytes.
FOXP3 is essential for regulatory T-cell production and normal function.
CD40L-CD40 signaling is required for B-cell class switching beyond IgM.
